title: Why Do Mosquitoes Bite YOU More? 🦟
description:
It's probably not your "sweet blood". Mosquitoes follow the carbon dioxide in your breath from about 30 feet away, then choose by smell. In a 2022 Rockefeller University study, the people mosquitoes loved most had far more oily carboxylic acids on their skin. One volunteer was 100 times more attractive than another, and stayed that way for years. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

Scientists think those acids are the main lure, but the study shows a link, not final proof, and it tested one species (Aedes aegypti). The cheese part is real too: in a 1990s experiment that later won an Ig Nobel Prize, malaria mosquitoes went for Limburger cheese as much as for human feet. Garlic and vitamin B have been tested and do not keep them away; a registered insect repellent does. Next up: why time flies as you get older.
